text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementEvolutionWas This Neanderthal Murdered?A prehistoric cold caseJCBy Jake Currie10:00 AM CDT on October 15, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleThe Shanidar Cave system in Iraq provided some of the first evidence that Neanderthals, like us, buried their dead. Now, according to a new study published in Scientific Reports, it might also be the site of a prehistoric murder mystery. Powered By 10 ShareNextStayWithin the cave, archaeologists found a scapula (shoulder blade) buried underneath 25 feet of rock belonging to a roughly 45-year-old Neanderthal man who lived around 75,000 years ago called Shanidar A. This flat triangular bone is relatively thin, and Shanidar A’s had a circular hole a little wider than half an inch in his—a puncture wound.
